overview: IWorldAccess bridge between WorldServer events and ServerConfigurationManager broadcasts. Applies volume-scaled and fixed radii with dimension gating. Forwards block updates to PlayerManager chunk map. Manages entity tracker add/remove.

methods.detail: Uses sendToAllNear with radius 16.0D, or 16.0F*volume if volume>1.0F. Gated by theWorldServer dimension ID. Creates S29PacketSoundEffect with pos, volume, pitch.
methods.name: playSound
methods.purpose: Broadcast named sound with volume-scaled range.

methods.detail: Same radius rule as playSound: 16.0D or 16*volume. Calls sendToAllNearExcept for originator exclusion. Dimension-gated. Used for player-caused sounds.
methods.name: playSoundToNearExcept

methods.detail: Calls sendToAllNearExcept with fixed 64.0D radius and dimension gate. Sends S28PacketEffect with sfxType, BlockPos, data, false. Excludes triggering player.
methods.name: playAuxSFX
methods.purpose: Broadcast block auxiliary effect near position except actor.

methods.detail: Calls sendPacketToAllPlayers with S28PacketEffect soundID, pos, data, true. No distance or dimension gating. Used for portal, wither spawn style events.
methods.name: broadcastSound
methods.purpose: Global broadcast of auxiliary effect to all players.

methods.detail: Iterates configuration manager player list, filters worldObj==theWorldServer and ID!=breakerId. Checks d2<1024.0D (32 blocks). Sends S25PacketBlockBreakAnim directly.
methods.name: sendBlockBreakProgress
methods.purpose: Send crack animation to viewers within 32 blocks.

methods.detail: Delegates to PlayerManager.markBlockForUpdate mapping BlockPos to chunk. No immediate packet; PlayerInstance.onUpdate later picks S23/S22/S21 by count. Chunk-scoped fan-out.
methods.name: markBlockForUpdate
methods.purpose: Queue chunk block change for batched send.

methods.detail: Calls theWorldServer.getEntityTracker.trackEntity. Tracker later emits spawn packets per type. No direct packet here. Entry point for entity spawn fan-out.
methods.name: onEntityAdded
methods.purpose: Register new entity with tracker for visibility.

methods.detail: Calls EntityTracker.untrackEntity then Scoreboard.func_181140_a. Causes destroy packets via tracker. No radius; removes from all viewers.
methods.name: onEntityRemoved
methods.purpose: Untrack entity and clear scoreboard state.

internal_fields.name: theWorldServer
internal_fields.role: Source dimension ID and PlayerManager/Tracker access

internal_fields.name: IWorldAccess
internal_fields.role: Interface hooking world events to network fan-out

methods_detailed.name: playSound
methods_detailed.detail_long: This IWorldAccess hook broadcasts a named sound to nearby players in the same dimension. It is called by world simulation when a block or entity emits a sound. It resolves recipients via ServerConfigurationManager.sendToAllNear at the exact x y z origin. The radius rule is volume scaled: 16.0D by default, or 16.0F times volume when volume exceeds 1.0F. This lets loud sounds like explosions or withers travel farther than quiet clicks. Dimension gating uses theWorldServer.provider.getDimensionId so nether and overworld do not cross hear. The packet is S29PacketSoundEffect built from sound name, position, volume, and pitch. No exclusion applies, so even the causing player hears it. This contrasts with playSoundToNearExcept and the fixed 64.0D aux path.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The comment documents soundName position volume pitch args. The method signature binds those plus coordinates. The single body line calls sendToAllNear with volume ternary for radius. The dimension ID arg gates by world. The S29PacketSoundEffect constructor packs name, coords, volume, pitch. This is inclusive broadcast with scaled 16.0D base radius.

methods_detailed.name: playSoundToNearExcept
methods_detailed.detail_long: This variant broadcasts the same named sound but excludes one originator player. It follows the identical volume-scaled radius rule as playSound. When volume is above 1.0F the radius becomes 16.0F times volume, otherwise fixed 16.0D. Recipients are resolved with sendToAllNearExcept passing the except EntityPlayer reference. Dimension gating again uses theWorldServer dimension ID to prevent cross-dimension hearing. The packet is S29PacketSoundEffect with identical sound name, x y z, volume, and pitch fields. This is used for player-caused sounds where the actor plays the sound locally or should not double hear. All other nearby players in range still receive it. The only difference from playSound is the exclusion filter.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The comment states the except-player behavior. The signature adds the except EntityPlayer first arg. The body mirrors playSound but calls sendToAllNearExcept. The ternary preserves 16.0D versus 16.0F times volume scaling. The S29PacketSoundEffect args are unchanged. This shows exclusion plus dimension-gated radius filtering.

methods_detailed.name: playAuxSFX
methods_detailed.detail_long: This hook broadcasts a block auxiliary effect such as dispenser click or record break near a position. It excludes the triggering EntityPlayer passed in, so that player does not get a duplicate local effect. Recipients are resolved via sendToAllNearExcept with the block position coordinates. The radius is fixed at 64.0D regardless of volume, wider than the 16.0D base sound radius. Dimension gating uses theWorldServer dimension ID. The packet is S28PacketEffect constructed with sfxType, BlockPos, data, and false for non-global flag. The data field carries block ID or extra info depending on sfxType. This contrasts with broadcastSound which is global with true flag. Only players within 64 blocks in the same dimension receive it.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The empty playRecord stub shows no networking for records here. The playAuxSFX signature binds actor, type, pos, and data. The body calls sendToAllNearExcept with 64.0D fixed radius and dimension gate. The S28PacketEffect is built with type, BlockPos, data, and false. The false flag marks it as ranged not global. This is exclusion plus fixed-radius fan-out.

methods_detailed.name: broadcastSound
methods_detailed.detail_long: This method sends an auxiliary effect to every connected player with no range limit. It does not use sendToAllNear or any 16.0D or 64.0D or 512.0D radius check. It calls sendPacketToAllPlayers directly so all dimensions hear it unless client filters. The packet is S28PacketEffect built from soundID, BlockPos, data, and true for global flag. The true flag distinguishes it from playAuxSFX ranged effects. Typical uses are wither spawn, ender dragon death, or portal events that need world-wide awareness. Because there is no dimension gating, overworld players can receive nether-originated global events. No exclusion applies, so the trigger player also receives it. This is the loudest scope in WorldManager.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The signature takes sound ID, position, and data. The single body line calls sendPacketToAllPlayers with no radius. The S28PacketEffect constructor uses true to mark global broadcast. The following lines reveal the start of sendBlockBreakProgress loop. This contrast shows global versus ranged S28 usage. No dimension or distance filtering occurs here.

methods_detailed.name: sendBlockBreakProgress
methods_detailed.detail_long: This method streams block cracking animation stages to nearby viewers. It loops over every EntityPlayerMP in the configuration manager player list. For each candidate it first checks worldObj identity equals theWorldServer to enforce dimension separation. It then skips the breaker entity ID itself so the miner does not receive their own crack echo. It computes dx dy dz from block pos to player posX posY posZ. It checks squared distance less than 1024.0D which equals 32 blocks. Only qualifiers get a direct S25PacketBlockBreakAnim via playerNetServerHandler.sendPacket. The packet carries breakerId, BlockPos, and progress 0 to 9 or negative to clear. Each progress change sends a fresh packet with no batching. This tight 32 block scope keeps digging visuals local.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The signature binds breaker ID, position, and stage. The for loop iterates the global player list. The if filters null, same worldObj, and non-breaker ID. The dx dy dz lines compute offset for squared distance. The less than 1024.0D check gates to 32 blocks. The sendPacket line builds S25PacketBlockBreakAnim with ID, pos, and progress. This is manual per-player distance filtering.

methods_detailed.name: markBlockForUpdate
methods_detailed.detail_long: This is the server hook that queues a block change for chunk-scoped delivery. On the client the sibling does render updates, but on the server it only flags the chunk. It delegates to theWorldServer.getPlayerManager with markBlockForUpdate and BlockPos. No packet is constructed or sent immediately here. PlayerManager maps the position to chunk XZ via right shift 4 and finds the PlayerInstance. That instance records local coordinates and defers the packet choice to onUpdate next tick. A single flagged block later becomes S23, two to sixty three become S22, and sixty four trigger S21 full chunk. Only players watching that chunk receive the eventual flush. This indirection enables per-tick batching instead of per-setBlock spam.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The comment describes the client render range behavior. The empty markBlockRangeForRenderUpdate shows no server networking. The markBlockForUpdate signature takes only BlockPos. The body delegates to PlayerManager markBlockForUpdate. No radius or S23 S22 S21 construction appears here. This proves queuing is deferred to PlayerInstance onUpdate batching.

methods_detailed.name: onEntityAdded
methods_detailed.detail_long: This IWorldAccess callback registers a newly loaded or spawned entity for visibility tracking. It is invoked on all world accesses when an entity enters the world. On the server it calls theWorldServer.getEntityTracker with trackEntity and the entity. The tracker creates an EntityTrackerEntry that later emits the correct spawn packet per entity type. No packet is sent synchronously inside this method, so no radius like 512.0D applies yet. Viewer assignment uses tracking ranges configured per entity class. This is the entry point that eventually leads to spawn packet fan-out. Without this call clients would never learn about the entity. It complements onEntityRemoved which tears down tracking.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The comment contrasts client texture versus server tracker behavior. The method signature takes the new Entity. The single body line calls EntityTracker trackEntity. No packet constructor or radius appears inline. Tracking ranges are applied inside the tracker later. This shows deferred spawn fan-out via tracker entries.

methods_detailed.name: onEntityRemoved
methods_detailed.detail_long: This callback tears down server visibility when an entity unloads or dies. It first calls theWorldServer.getEntityTracker with untrackEntity for the entity. That causes the tracker to send destroy packets and remove the entry from all viewers. It then calls theWorldServer.getScoreboard with func_181140_a to clear any scoreboard state tied to the entity. No distance radius governs removal because all current viewers must forget the entity. No explicit packet constructor appears here since destroy packets originate inside the tracker. This ensures clients do not retain ghost entities. It is the symmetric counterpart to onEntityAdded registration.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The comment describes unload versus destroy handling. The signature takes the removed Entity. The first body line calls untrackEntity to trigger destroy fan-out. The second line clears scoreboard objectives for that entity. No 16.0D or 64.0D check is present. Removal is broadcast to all prior viewers. This shows cleanup without direct packet code.
